title: Launch Corridor Gatekeeper: Dynamic Capacity Hedge & Runway Conductor
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Launches across runtime / console / API frequently collide on shared capacity windows and stakeholder bandwidth. Current release windows are statically allocated which leads to last-minute hedging, uncoordinated burst requests, and risk of latency SLO violations during multi-surface launches.

Goal: Design and deliver a 'Launch Corridor Gatekeeper' product-level conductor that coordinates launch runway reservations, applies dynamic capacity hedging policies, and enforces a deterministic interlock protocol between runtime, console, and API teams. The conductor is intended to reduce last-minute capacity churn, provide clear escalation lanes, and surface objective go/no-go signals to PM/Eng/Infra.

Scope (MVP):
- A runway reservation API (Console + PM facing) to request time windows, capacity bands (low/medium/high), and prioritization tags.
- Hedging policy engine (policy definitions only in MVP) that suggests reserve amounts based on historical traffic, model rollout impact, and targeted SLO buffers.
- Interlock checklist and signal thresholds (traffic replay plan, safety margins, rollback gates) surfaced in Console release page.
- Automated alerting rules and a simple escalation playbook to notify infra on hedges that exceed capacity guardrails.
- Documentation and stakeholder runbooks for how to reserve, contest, and release capacity lanes.

Out-of-scope (MVP): automated capacity allocation to Dedicated pools, deep telemetry ingestion pipeline, and per-customer SLA negotiation flows. These are follow-ups for Q3.

Why this matters: Reduces the frequency of ad-hoc capacity requests by infra and minimizes surprises that push teams into emergency rollbacks. Creates a single source of truth for who owns a launch window and what hedges are in place.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation API prototype for creating, updating, and canceling runway reservations (CRUD) is available and documented
Gatekeeper UI panel added to Console release page showing active reservations and hedges
Hedging policy templates (3: conservative, baseline, aggressive) defined and stored as versioned policy artifacts
On-call escalation path documented and automated PagerDuty/Slack notifications wired for over-hedge events
Launch checklist with explicit SLO gates (latency, error budget, tail latency thresholds) appears in the release page and can be marked by owners
Stakeholder sign-off from runtime, console, and API leads following staged demo
progress_updates: 2025-11-12: Initial discovery workshop with runtime, console, and infra teams; mapped current launch lifecycle and pain points (Aisha)
2025-12-02: Prioritization review; agreed MVP scope and deferred automated allocation to Q3 (Diego)
2026-01-18: Prototype Reservation API contract drafted and posted to Confluence: /confluence/redwood/launch-corridor/reservation-api (link below) (PM team)
2026-02-07: Runtime team provided traffic distribution heuristics and historical launch spikes; product updated hedging model assumptions (runtime-eng@redwood)
2026-02-28: Console team mockups completed for gatekeeper panel; usability review scheduled for 2026-03-12
2026-03-10: Exec sponsor (Head of Product) approved pilot with two upcoming launches; assigned Diego as release conductor and two SRE liaisons (Diego)
Next: Build reservation CRUD API, wire minimal persistence, and implement Console panel backend integration (Sprint 2026-W11)
Blockers: Need final roadmap dates from Dedicated team for two pilot launches; awaiting confirmed dates (dependency)
Customer impact: Medium — internal-facing coordination to reduce downstream runtime incidents
decisions: Keep initial hedging as policy-only (no auto-scaling actions) to minimize blast radius
Use existing Console auth and feature-flag framework for gated rollout of Gatekeeper UI
Persist reservations as a lightweight Dynamo-style record in infra namespace to avoid schema migrations in MVP
Integrate alerts via existing release-health Slack channel and PagerDuty instead of building a new ops channel
